arxiv-2106-08836.title: Axion clouds may survive the perturbative tidal interaction over the early inspiral phase of black hole binaries
arxiv-2106-08836.creator: and Takahiro Tanaka
arxiv-2106-08836.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by and Takahiro Tanaka. Gravitational wave observation has the potential of probing ultralight bosonic fields such as axions. Axions form a cloud around a rotating black hole (BH) by superradiant instability and should affect the gravitational waveform from binary BHs. On the other hand, considering the cloud associated with a BH in a binary system, tidal interaction depletes the cloud in some cases during the inspiral phase.

arxiv-2110-13284.title: A New Method for Estimating Starspot Lifetimes Based on Autocorrelation Functions
arxiv-2110-13284.creator: Gibor Basri, Tristan Streichenberger, Connor McWard, Lawrence Edmond IV, Joanne Tan, Minjoo Lee, Trey Melton
arxiv-2110-13284.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Gibor Basri, Tristan Streichenberger, Connor McWard, Lawrence Edmond IV, Joanne Tan, Minjoo Lee, Trey Melton. We present a method that utilizes autocorrelation functions from long-term precision broadband differential light curves to estimate the average lifetimes of starspot groups for two large sample of Kepler stars: stars with and without previously known rotation periods. Our method is calibrated by comparing the strengths of the first few normalized autocorrelation peaks using ensembles of models that have various starspot lifetimes.

arxiv-2201-00168.creator: Jiang Liu \aref amss,amss1,hit2, Meihua Zhong \aref amss,hit, Huanhuan Chen \aref hit
arxiv-2201-00168.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Jiang Liu \aref amss,amss1,hit2, Meihua Zhong \aref amss,hit, Huanhuan Chen \aref hit. arxiv-2202-00893.title: Mold into a Graph: Efficient Bayesian Optimization over Mixed-Spaces
arxiv-2202-00893.creator: Jaeyeon Ahn, Taehyeon Kim, Se-young Yun
arxiv-2202-00893.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Jaeyeon Ahn, Taehyeon Kim, Se-young Yun. Real-world optimization problems are generally not just black-box problems, but also involve mixed types of inputs in which discrete and continuous variables coexist. Such mixed-space optimization possesses the primary challenge of modeling complex interactions between the inputs. In this work, we propose a novel yet simple approach that entails exploiting the graph data structure to model the underlying relationship between variables, i.e., variables as nodes and interactions defined by edges.

arxiv-2207-11902.title: Modeling the Charge Collection Efficiency in the Li-diffused Inactive Layer of P-type High Purity Germanium Detector
arxiv-2207-11902.creator: W.H. Dai, H. Ma, Q. Yue, L.T. Yang, Z. Zeng, J.P. Cheng, J.L Li
arxiv-2207-11902.description: Abstract A model of the Li-diffused inactive layer in P-type high purity germanium detectors is built to describe the transportation of charge carriers and calculate the charge collection efficiency therein. The model is applied to calculate charge collection efficiency of a P-type point-contact germanium detector used in rare event physics experiments and validated in another P-type semi-planar germanium detector.

arxiv-2211-14584.title: Intermediate β \beta -shifts as greedy β \beta -shifts with a hole
arxiv-2211-14584.creator: Niels Langeveld, Tony Samuel
arxiv-2211-14584.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Niels Langeveld, Tony Samuel. We show that every intermediate β \beta -transformation is topologically conjugate to a greedy β \beta -transformation with a hole at zero, and provide a counterexample illustrating that the correspondence is not one-to-one .

arxiv-2401-05590.title: Free-floating “planets” in the macrolensed quasar Q2237+0305 2023 Free-floating “planets” in the macrolensed quasar Q2237+0305 – 15
arxiv-2401-05590.creator: Artem V. Tuntsov, Geraint F. Lewis, Mark A. Walker
arxiv-2401-05590.description: Abstract It has been claimed that the variability of field quasars resembles gravitational lensing by a large cosmological population of free-floating planets with mass ∼ 10 ​ M ⊕ \sim 10\,{\rm M}_{\oplus} . But Galactic photometric monitoring experiments, on the other hand, exclude a large population of such planetary-mass gravitational lenses.

arxiv-2401-12932.title: Segmentation of tibiofemoral joint tissues from knee MRI using MtRA-Unet and incorporating shape information: Data from the Osteoarthritis Initiative
arxiv-2401-12932.creator: Akshay Daydar, Alik Pramanick, Arijit Sur, Subramani Kanagaraj
arxiv-2401-12932.description: Abstract Knee Osteoarthritis (KOA) is the third most prevalent Musculoskeletal Disorder (MSD) after neck and back pain. To monitor such a severe MSD, a segmentation map of the femur, tibia and tibiofemoral cartilage is usually accessed using the automated segmentation algorithm from the Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) of the knee.

arxiv-2408-13097.title: An Update on the Classification of Rank 2 Weak Fano Threefolds
arxiv-2408-13097.creator: Joseph W. Cutrone, Nicholas A. Marshburn
arxiv-2408-13097.description: Abstract . In this paper, an update on the classification of smooth weak Fano threefolds with Picard number two and small anti-canonical maps is given. Geometric constructions are provided for previously open numerical cases by blowing up certain curves on smooth Fano threefolds of Picard number one.

arxiv-2504-18721.title: High energy extragalactic multimessenger backgrounds from starburst and dead galaxies
arxiv-2504-18721.creator: Ellis R. Owen 1,2, Yoshiyuki Inoue 1,3,4, Tatsuki Fujiwara 1 and Albert K. H. Kong 5 1 Theoretical Astrophysics, Department of Earth and Space Science, Graduate School of Science, The University of Osaka, Toyonaka 560-0043, Osaka, Japan 2 Astrophysical Big Bang Laboratory (ABBL), RIKEN Pioneering Re
arxiv-2504-18721.description: Abstract Starburst galaxies are γ \gamma -ray sources. Canonically, their emission is driven by hadronic cosmic rays (CRs) interacting with interstellar gas, forming γ \gamma -rays via the decay of neutral pions. Charged pions are also formed in this process. They decay into secondary leptons, including electrons and neutrinos.

arxiv-2505-22589.title: On dual regime in Yang-Baxter deformed O ⁡ ( 2 ​ N ) \mathrm{O}(2N) sigma models
arxiv-2505-22589.creator: Alexey Bychkov, Alexey Litvinov 1. Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology, 121205 Moscow, Russia 2. HSE University, 6 Usacheva str., Moscow 119048, Russia
arxiv-2505-22589.description: Abstract In this paper, we explore a new class of integrable sigma models, which we refer to as the ”dual regime” of Yang-Baxter (YB) deformed O ⁡ ( 2 ​ N ) \mathrm{O}(2N) sigma models. This dual regime manifests itself in the conformal perturbation approach.

arxiv-2506-02751.title: RobustSplat: Decoupling Densification and Dynamics for Transient-Free 3DGS
arxiv-2506-02751.creator: Chuanyu Fu, Yuqi Zhang, Kunbin Yao, Guanying Chen, Yuan Xiong, Chuan Huang, Shuguang Cui, Xiaochun Cao
arxiv-2506-02751.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Chuanyu Fu, Yuqi Zhang, Kunbin Yao, Guanying Chen, Yuan Xiong, Chuan Huang, Shuguang Cui, Xiaochun Cao. 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has gained significant attention for its real-time, photo-realistic rendering in novel-view synthesis and 3D modeling. However, existing methods struggle with accurately modeling scenes affected by transient objects, leading to artifacts in the rendered images. We identify that the Gaussian densification process, while enhancing scene detail capture, unintentionally contributes to these artifacts by growing additional Gaussians that model transient disturbances.

arxiv-2507-04051.title: Generate, Refine, and Encode: Leveraging Synthesized Novel Samples for On-the-Fly Fine-Grained Category Discovery
arxiv-2507-04051.creator: Xiao Liu, Nan Pu, Haiyang Zheng, Wenjing Li, Nicu Sebe, Zhun Zhong
arxiv-2507-04051.description: Abstract In this paper, we investigate a practical yet challenging task: On-the-fly Category Discovery (OCD). This task focuses on the online identification of newly arriving stream data that may belong to both known and unknown categories, utilizing the category knowledge from only labeled data. Existing OCD methods are devoted to fully mining transferable knowledge from only labeled data.

pmc-10536558.title: FS-RSDD: Few-Shot Rail Surface Defect Detection with Prototype Learning
pmc-10536558.creator: Yongzhi Min, Ziwei Wang, Yang Liu, Zheng Wang, Yi Qin
pmc-10536558.description: As an important component of the railway system, the surface damage that occurs on the rails due to daily operations can pose significant safety hazards. This paper proposes a simple yet effective rail surface defect detection model, FS-RSDD, for rail surface condition monitoring, which also aims to address the issue of insufficient defect samples faced by previous detection models.

pmc-10655394.title: Food-grade titanium dioxide and zinc oxide nanoparticles induce toxicity and cardiac damage after oral exposure in rats
pmc-10655394.creator: Manuel Alejandro Herrera-Rodríguez, María del Pilar Ramos-Godinez, Agustina Cano-Martínez, Francisco Correa Segura, Angélica Ruiz-Ramírez, Natalia Pavón, Elizabeth Lira-Silva, Rocío Bautista-Pérez, Rosina Sánchez Thomas, Norma Laura Delgado-Buenrostro, Yolanda Irasema Chirino, Rebeca López-Marure
pmc-10655394.description: BackgroundMetallic nanoparticles (NPs) are widely used as food additives for human consumption. NPs reach the bloodstream given their small size, getting in contact with all body organs and cells. NPs have adverse effects on the respiratory and intestinal tract; however, few studies have focused on the toxic consequences of orally ingested metallic NPs on the cardiovascular system.

pmc-11620809.title: Challenges and Innovations in Breast Cancer Screening in India: A Review of Epidemiological Trends and Diagnostic Strategies
pmc-11620809.creator: Induni Nayodhara Weerarathna, Anurag Luharia, Ashish Uke, Gaurav Mishra
pmc-11620809.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The intricate terrain of breast cancer (BC) in India is examined in this review, which also looks at screening techniques, geographical differences, epidemiological trends, and obstacles to early diagnosis. BC has a major impact in India, especially on women. The research examines data from 2014 to 2024 and finds that, although overall cancer rates are declining, there has been a noticeable increase in BC cases.

pmc-11691881.title: PUBLIC ATTITUDES TOWARD PHYSICIAN-ASSISTED DYING: A CROSS-SECTIONAL SURVEY IN TAIWAN
pmc-11691881.creator: Duan-Rung Chen, Kevin Chien-Chang Wu, Chun-Tung Kuo
pmc-11691881.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). PurposeThis study aims to assess public attitudes towards Physician-Assisted Dying (PAD) in Taiwan, where legal support for PAD is notably absent despite its public endorsement in broader Asia, including Japan, South Korea, and China. Method: Utilizing an online survey, we gathered data from 3,922 Taiwanese adults from August to November 2022 to evaluate their support for PAD across different contexts: terminal illnesses, unbearable non-terminal pain, and severe cognitive impairments.

pmc-12430575.title: Antioxidant Capacity, Volatile Profile, and Physical Properties Changes of Kohlrabi Treated with Onion and Beetroot Juices Using Vacuum Impregnation Process
pmc-12430575.creator: Magdalena Kręcisz, Marta Klemens, Joanna Kolniak-Ostek, Bogdan Stępień, Maciej Combrzyński, Aleks Latański
pmc-12430575.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The aim of the study was to use vacuum impregnation (VI) with onion and beetroot juices as a pre-treatment before drying to develop innovative dried kohlrabi products. Two modern drying techniques were used: freeze-drying (FD) and vacuum drying (VD). The physicochemical properties were determined, including color, water activity, dry matter, density, volumetric gel index, texture, antioxidant capacity, total phenolic content (TPC), and volatile organic compounds (VOCs). It was shown that vacuum impregnation reduced the color lightness and springiness of kohlrabi.

pmc-12575849.title: Condensation-dependent interactome of a chromatin remodeler underlies tumor suppressor activities
pmc-12575849.creator: Yasuhiro Tsukamoto, Atsuki Kawamura, Ayhan Yurtsever, Hidefumi Suzuki, Nichole Marcela Rojas-Chaverra, Hiroki Sato, Daisuke Ino, Takehiko Ichikawa, Weilin Wei, Shojiro Haji, Dominic Chih-Cheng Voon, Akinobu Matsumoto, Kunio Matsumoto, Hidehisa Takahashi, Noriyuki Kodera, Takeshi Fukuma, Yoshihiro Og
pmc-12575849.description: Chromatin remodelers are vital for cellular functions like transcription by modulating nucleosome accessibility. Although biological condensates regulate these processes, the contribution of chromatin remodelers to condensation mechanisms remains poorly understood. Here, we examine the role of the E1321 frameshift mutation in CHD1, a chromatin remodeler, which is often targeted in cancers.

pmc-12654221.title: The Monotonic Behavior of Existing Bridge Piers Retrofitted by Expansive Concrete-Filled Steel Tubes: An Experimental and Numerical Study
pmc-12654221.creator: Ganghui Peng, Guowen Yao, Hongyu Jia, Yun Yao, Shixiong Zheng, Raffaele Landolfo
pmc-12654221.description: With the growing traffic volume in China, numerous existing highway bridges in seismic zones are constrained by outdated design standards that are inadequate against current seismic requirements. To address this issue, this study proposes a novel reinforcement technique using expansive concrete-filled steel tube (ECFST) for bridge piers.

pmc-13030710.title: From Gut to Systemic Circulation: Molecular Strategies of Botulinum Neurotoxin Complexes
pmc-13030710.creator: Juliette Mondy, Emmanuel Lemichez
pmc-13030710.description: Botulinum neurotoxins (BoNTs), among the most potent biological toxins, rely on co-produced nontoxic proteins to survive harsh gastrointestinal conditions and achieve efficient systemic dissemination after oral exposure. Recent structural and functional studies have revealed how BoNTs bind to the nontoxic non-hemagglutinin (NTNH) factors to engage in interactions with either OrfXs/P47 or hemagglutinins (HAs) components for systemic dissemination.

pmc-13236523.title: Type B insulin resistance with glycemic extremes: a case report and literature review
pmc-13236523.creator: Emmeline Monique T. Ngo, Jordan M. Rowe, Thilo Samson Chillon, Lutz Schomburg, Rebecca J Brown, Shourya Tadisina
pmc-13236523.description: BackgroundType B insulin resistance (TBIR) is a rare autoimmune disorder caused by immunoglobulin G (IgG) autoantibodies targeting the insulin receptor. These antibodies act as partial agonists, resulting in severe insulin resistance and hyperglycemia at high titer, and hypoglycemia at low titer. TBIR typically affects middle-aged women with autoimmune diseases but may occur in younger individuals and across diverse ethnic groups.

pmc-13270864.title: Do subjective and objective baseline sleep disturbances predict post-traumatic stress disorder treatment response? A secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial
pmc-13270864.creator: Salomé Porten, Franziska Friedmann, Nikola Schoofs, Philip Santangelo, Ulrich Ebner-Priemer, Meike Müller-Engelmann, Regina Steil, Nikolaus Kleindienst, Thomas Fydrich, Kathlen Priebe

pmc-13305056.title: Repurposing Resmetirom to Suppress MASLD/MASH-HCC in the Dysmetabolic Era
pmc-13305056.creator: Amedeo Lonardo, Ming-Hua Zheng, Ralf Weiskirchen
pmc-13305056.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Metabolic disorders are risk factors for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) through complex proinflammatory, molecular, and cellular processes within a systemic dysmetabolic milieu. Despite significant advancements in the last two decades, HCC remains a challenging condition to treat. Resmetirom is a liver‑directed, selective THR‑β agonist that enhances mitochondrial β-oxidation, reduces de novo lipogenesis, improves lipid and cholesterol homeostasis, and, in preclinical HCC associated with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease/steatohepatitis (MASLD/MASH-HCC) models, attenuates midkine/lipoprotein receptor-related protein 1 (MDK/LRP1)-mediated immunosuppressive crosstalk.

pmc-13402939.title: Rapid Extensively Drug‐Resistant (XDR) TB Diagnosis: An In‐House DNA Biochip for Drug Resistance Detection and Mutation Profiling of Mycobacterium tuberculosis
pmc-13402939.creator: Bharti Jain, Savita Kulkarni, Nawab Singh Baghel

pmc-13554373.title: A State‐Gated Metallo‐DNAzyme Framework Programs Tumor Stress Vulnerability Through Metabolic Licensing
pmc-13554373.creator: Xiaodong Ma, Lingyun He, Xinru Wang, Yuanyuan Wei, Chengcheng Li, Jiaqi Yan, Weijian Sun, Xian Shen, Hongbo Zhang
pmc-13554373.description: Stress‐generating therapeutic materials are commonly optimized to deliver cytotoxic inputs, but delivery alone does not determine whether intracellular stress becomes irreversible damage. Tumor cells can buffer metal‐, redox‐ and mitochondrial stress through glucose‐dependent metabolism, creating a gap between stress exposure and stress execution.

pmc-13576333.title: Bidirectional pathways to suicide: how parent-child interactions shape adolescent depression and suicidality in China
pmc-13576333.creator: Yan Han, Rongying Sun, Yan Tang, Chunhong Wei
pmc-13576333.description: BackgroundAdolescent suicide, largely driven by depression, is a critical public health crisis in China, with depression affecting over 70% of cases and demonstrating recurrence rates exceeding 80% within one year. While parent-child interactions significantly influence suicidal trajectories, existing research has predominantly examined unidirectional perspectives, neglecting the complex bidirectional dynamics between adolescents and their caregivers.

pmc-13601684.title: A Framework for the Estimation of Quality-Adjusted Life-Years Using Joint Models of Longitudinal and Survival Data
pmc-13601684.creator: Michael J Crowther, Alessandro Gasparini, Sara Ekberg, Federico Felizzi, Elaine Gallagher, Noman Paracha
pmc-13601684.description: Background:Length and quality of life are frequently combined in health technology assessments to derive a single, generic measure of health improvement due to a treatment or medicine. One such measure is given by quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), typically calculated assuming discrete health states and quality-of-life values.

pmc-13685305.creator: Abdullah, Witaya Mathiyakom, Tsuyoshi Asai, Nasrullah Khan, Irfan Ullah, Anong Tantisuwat
pmc-13685305.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveThe primary objective was to compare the effects of aerobic and Pilates exercise programs on balance, gait performance, functional capacity, lower extremity strength, fear of falling, sleep quality, and quality of life in older adults.
